summary: Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy of Cu(111) islands on superconducting Nb(110) reveals Andreev bound-state spectra controlled by phase accumulation along confined surface-state trajectories. The zero-field excitation energy $E_0$ scales with trajectory length $\ell$ and the magnetic-field collapse scale $B_0 \propto 1/w$ with transverse projection, capturing geometry-tuned phase-coherent cavity physics.
motivation: Andreev cavities enable engineering of superconducting proximity spectra through phase-coherent electron-hole motion, but real-space local spectroscopy of extended two-dimensional cavities remains largely unexplored. Understanding how trajectory geometry shapes low-energy spectra in ballistic systems is relevant for phase-sensitive hybrid superconducting devices.
method: STM/STS measured proximitised Cu(111) surface states ($\Delta_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 0.92$ meV, $v_F \simeq 5.8 \times 10^5$ m/s) on Nb(110) films. Ray-traced trajectory ensembles extracted from STM topography were combined with a semiclassical Andreev bound-state condition incorporating dynamical phase $2E\ell/(\hbar v_F)$ and gauge-invariant magnetic phase bias $|\delta\varphi| \simeq 2\pi(\Phi_0/B) h_{\mathrm{eff}} w$ to simulate spectra.
result: Across seven islands, $E_0$ decreases with $\ell$ (range 175–624 nm) and $B_0$ decreases with $w$ (range 92–624 nm), both captured by the phase-accumulation model with $h_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 24$ nm. Out-of-plane field introduces vortex phase textures with spatial $\pi$-phase excursions across the island, demonstrating sensitivity to condensate-phase winding.
